structure: Connecticut Elementary and Secondary Social Studies Standards (2023), organized by grade K-8 and three HS courses (Modern World History, United States History III, Civics and Government; no grade tie, grades 9-12). Front matter (credits, TOC, acknowledgments, introduction, Inquiry Arc background, organization/coding explanation with Figures 1-2, K-12 sequence table) precedes each section. Each grade/course section has: title line ('Grade N: Name' or 'High School: Name'), overview narrative, 'Organization of ... Standards' note, Course Questions (bullets), Course Topics (numbered), '<Grade> Inquiry Standards' with an Inquiry Arc graphic, then 'students will...' with Dimension 1-4 headings and inquiry standards coded G.Inq.D.x (e.g. 3.Inq.1.a; MW/US/CG.Inq for HS), each followed by CT Core Standards (CCSS) references and key academic vocabulary; then '<Grade> Content Standards' with intro and Dimension 2 graphic, 'students will...' and topic headings ('• 3-1. Topic name') listing content standards coded G.Lens.skill.x (Civ, Eco, Geo, His; e.g. 5.Civ.3.a; MW-1 / US-1 / CG-1 topic numbering for HS) with parenthetical e.g. content suggestions inside the standard. Grades come from section headings and code prefixes.

issues: u639: Grade 3 topic 3-1 content standards (3.Civ.1.a through 3.Eco.12.a, 10+ standards) are merged into a single unit by extraction; labeled standards, grade 3.
u152-u153: 'Social Studies Content Themes' graphic (six themes) is an image; only the caption text is extracted. Labeled backup.
u250-u285 (Figures 1 and 2): coding-structure figures extracted as fragments (table cells, key numbers, sample codes 5.Inq.3.a, 5.Civ.3.a); labeled backup as how-to-read material.

u763, u765, u871, u873, u1067, u1069: Grade 5, 6 and 8 course questions and course topics are each merged into one unit (bullets/numbers run together); labeled examples (questions) and standards (topics).
u216-u245: K-12 sequence table (course/topic lists for K-8 and HS) is a front-matter overview; labeled backup, grades all, not as per-grade standards.

State guide lists HS courses as Modern World History, US History III, Civics and Government; document titles them 'Modern World History', 'United States History III' and 'Civics and Government' (course strings use these). HS inquiry standards are course-specific (MW/US/CG.Inq) so they carry the course name rather than course null.

Content standards are listed under topics but codes are not ordered; some standards sit under a topic whose theme differs from their strand (e.g., 4.Geo.5.b after 4.His.9.a in topic 4-2). Topic from heading position only.
Content standards whose text contains 'e.g.' lists are labeled standards (unit not split). 'CT Core Standards' CCSS literacy references labeled backup; 'Key academic vocabulary' labeled examples.

u1208-u1211 and other HS standards: text is split across two x-positioned units (code at x=67, text at x=129-135); both halves labeled with same category. Some codes (e.g., u1259, u1424, u1440) are separated from their text unit.
Extraction artefacts inside standard text (hyphenation/spacing breaks such as 'com munity', 'environ mental', 'Ameri can') in many units; not corrected, no impact on labeling.
